method.grid: stitched tile.raw, 1 tile = 100 world units = 1 m = 1 half-cell
method.dedither: open(3x3) then close(3x3), then drop components < 30 tiles
method.path_rule: index is path-role when its art family is one of ['dirt', 'paved', 'sand', 'rock'] AND it is not the base layer AND coverage <= 0.40 AND solid_retention >= 0.25 AND median corridor width in [2.0, 16.0] m AND aspect (L^2/area) >= 10 AND ribbon_fraction >= 0.60
method.spur_pruning: dead-end branches under 10 m are removed from the medial axis before any topology is counted
method.road_verdict: shape alone also matches ribbon-shaped terrain, so a network counts as a road only when it is measurably flattened (slope_ratio < 0.60) AND has the block flag cleared (block_rate_ratio < 0.60) relative to a [6, 24] m control band

coordinates.tile_to_world_cm: x_cm = BasePosition.x + tile_x * 100, y_cm = BasePosition.y + tile_y * 100; tile (0,0) is the NW corner of sector 000000, X grows east and Y grows south
coordinates.caveat: areadata.txt stores object positions in MAP-LOCAL centimetres with Y NEGATED. The world_cm values here are absolute (they include BasePosition) and are NOT negated. To place a centreline vertex as an object you must therefore do BOTH steps: local_x = world_cm.x - BasePosition.x ; local_y = -(world_cm.y - BasePosition.y). Subtracting the base is not optional -- skipping it puts every object outside the map on any map whose BasePosition is non-zero, which is most of the corpus. See reference/mapformat/areadata-txt.md.
